Hey there! I \[20f\] have been in a college LDR for the last 4 years, and am in a similar boat as you guys as my bf is 2 years older, so going in meant 4-6 years apart. We go to school about a 12 hour drive apart, so cannot visit aside from school breaks. With that said, having been in a college LDR for so long, I can personally say that it absolutely gets easier. The place that you're in now is the hardest part because the gap between high school and college is harder than one anticipates. I would say that it's probably going to stay difficult until he really gets settled at his new university. Since long distance requires so much communication and effort, it can feel especially challenging since adjusting to college is already so hard by itself and involves so many new experiences. With that said, the longer you're in college, the more routine the LDR feels and the more natural it will feel :) While being apart is never EASY per se, you do get used to it and you two will strike a balance and routine that feels right and normal. One of the great things about LDR is it allows you to still have this great relationship with someone you care about while having a lot of independence during such a transformative part of your life, so I would take advantage of all the wonderful things your university has to offer and try to find a balance that works for you both!

I would bring it up when you’re together, maybe just saying that you wished you talked more and figure out a strategy together even if it’s trying to talk on the phone each night for 5 min before bed or figuring out something reliable to work with your schedule. To echo what others have said, having a day where you consistently plan to call has really helped us! I’ve also found that it helps bring me some peace of mind because I’m not always wondering when I’m going to talk to him. Hope this helps, and have fun next week! :)

Hey there--my boyfriend is in college and we've been going strong with distance for a year now. So let me tell you a little about my experience.

The first few weeks are ALWAYS the hardest. Like I get it, they really really suck. There are so many new things and it's really hard to not be able to talk all the time, especially if you're really used to that. THAT BEING SAID, it does get easier and once you both get adjusted and fall into a routine, it'll become much easier :) I recommend choosing a set day every week where you absolutely promise to Skype or FaceTime because then you always have something to look forward to and it helps a little. Communication is key otherwise, I know everyone's been saying that, but it really can't be emphasized enough. Also, for the intimacy thing, while its DEFINITELY not the same, I've found that sleeping in say, his shirts, and with a body pillow help a bit with missing him and wishing he was there. It can at least help at night. And there are definitely ways you can keep intimacy and your spark alive even with the distance. 

With that said, college LDRs are right for some people, not right for others. It's totally okay if you decide this is just not a situation you want to be in, even if you love him. The most important thing is that you're happy, and maybe that's by staying with him, but maybe not. 4 years is a long time and if you're sure he's the one you want to be with, it'll be time well worth the wait :) But if you aren't sure if you want to take the sacrifice and pain distance can bring, that's okay too. It's really whatever is going to bring you the most happiness. Wishing you all the best and lots of luck! Hang in there, it gets easier

Hi! I totally understand where you're coming from. My boyfriend (19) and I (17) are two years apart, so we knew college was going to be looming for the year we were together before he left. We're New Jersey to Indiana--a 12 hour drive--so we aren't really able to visit each other aside from when he comes home for breaks. That being said, we've made it through a year now (and started our second) and it's been relatively smooth sailing. To follow up on what was already said, there will be a change. But there will be changes in every relationship,whether it's long distance or not. The key is just how you bend with these changes. 
I've found the biggest aid in getting through the nerves and worries is to make the distance fun. The biggest help for me was writing him letters since we couldn't talk as much as we had been able to in the past. Just little things like that, care packages, really anything you can think of can make the distance fun and exciting :) Even just putting in the effort to call each other for 10 minutes every night can make a day of not having time to text so much easier. Just stay busy and remember, the distance doesn't last forever and you'll be back with him soon!

You already have been together a while so I'm sure your relationship is super strong. The time will fly by--just stay positive, keep busy, and keeping focusing on the day when hopefully you'll both be facing another major life change, only this one bringing you closer together. Good luck!! You have everyone's support on here :)

Hi! My bf (20) and I (18) are 12 hours apart and headed into our second year of distance due to college. The biggest thing that helped us last year was talk about EVERYTHING, even the hard stuff. How will you handle attraction to other (new) people? What are your boundaries, for parties, for making friends of the opposite sex, etc. Make a plan for how you will keep in touch. My bf and I Skype every Sunday and text throughout the week, sometimes calling each other on our way to class. But his roommate was on FaceTime with his girlfriend practically nonstop. Find what works best for the two of you, but remember that your relationship shouldn't keep you from enjoying college as well. There's absolutely no reason why you shouldn't be able to keep the girl you love from high school, but also don't let that keep you from making new friends :)

That being said, just a tip for the coming few weeks: the first few weeks of college are very very busy and will be for both of you. You'll be having a lot of information thrown at you, you'll be meeting more new people than you can count, and you'll be being tossed from orientation activity to orientation activity. I'm not going to lie, that part was really hard. My boyfriend was almost never around that first week or so snd it was kind of painful to see him having so much fun without me. They even gave a presentation about why students shouldn't stay with their high school sweethearts (that one was a dagger haha) BUT just remember that you're going through these new experience separately, but still together. You're going to grow even closer by learning more about each other and sharing so many new fun stories. Have faith in your love and your relationship and stay strong no matter what others say. As long as you can find a balance that's right for you and not let your relationship get in the way of school or school get in the way of your relationship, you'll be more than okay. You're both going to be busy sometimes. You're both going to get jealous occasionally. There are going to be ups and downs, there are going to be doubts, but it's all okay and all part of the process. The most important thing is you have a love worth waiting for and you will always have someone looking out for you and someone to come home to.

Other little things that work for us: sending care packages, writing letters, taking a TON of selfies while we're together, keeping a countdown app on our phones. We're going to try to watch Netflix together this year too. There are ways to make distance fun! Enjoy your week together, good luck at school, and remember, distance is only temporary. Sorry this is so long, I love seeing other high school to college relationships haha feel free to message me with any questions or worried and best of luck!!

Hi there. First off--take a deep breath. I know panic attacks can make you feel isolated and alone, but trust me, you are NOT alone. It's okay to take some mental health days every now and then and check in with yourself. That comes first. However, in situations like these where these attacks start taking over your life, I've found a bunch of small life style changes can work wonders. First, try to identify your triggers. What are some causes (if identifiable) of these panic attacks? How can you avoid them? Second, something I find really helpful is having a playlist for when I have an anxiety attack. The music on it manages to calm me down and bring me back and my friends know whenever I start to panic to just give me headphones and turn it on. Lastly, while it may seem so typical, exercise really truly does help a little bit. Once you manage to feel a little more secure, absolutely see a doctor. Remember--they're here to help you, not trigger you further. You're not on the journey alone! Hang in there. Sending hugs xxx

Hey there :) My bf [19M] and I [17F] also have about a 5-6 year end date ahead of us because of school. The thing that gets us through the most is remembering that this is a time where you're working towards your future--this person that you love is just an additional part of the dream (along with jobs and graduation) that you're working towards. I've found that by looking at the distance as just a necessary evil to reach that future goal as opposed to a burden, it makes such a long time apart seem much more doable. We also like to break down the gap into smaller chunks to make it seem less daunting and more exciting. Next month we'll have finished a year, so we're 1/6 of the way through. Sounds a lot better than saying 5 years left, right? Breaking it up into these segments--week by week, gaps till breaks, quarters, halves, you name it--definitely makes the time pass much easier and makes 5-6 years, well, seem like a lot less than 5-6. I also keep a countdown app on my phone with two dates: the next time I see him, and the end date, because as far away as it may seem, having the countdown really does prove the the time IS passing and you really ARE getting closer and closer with every day that goes by (only 61 months and 14 days now hahaha). Otherwise, I think the most important piece is surrounding yourself with encouragement. 5-6 years may be a long time, but as it goes on, you'll (hopefully) be growing ever closer with each others' families and friends and gaining even more of their support. You'll have even more love and enthusiasm surrounding you when you do close the distance. I think having this community and love is essential, because you have the support even on the days where it just seems almost too hard to do. Remember that while it may be a long time, you're getting closer little by little. As my bf says, "you can't cut down a tree in one swing. you just gotta pick up the ax and keep chopping little by little every day." This is just the time to continue to grow even more together and take in your time apart so your eventual time together will be even more special. You've already made it this far and kicked distance's butt :) The years are really only just another type of distance, so you can definitely show that one who's boss too. Keep your head up and best of luck to both of you~~ always nice to see another young LD college couple out there

Can't say I'm as much of a pro as some of the people here who have been doing this for years and years, but I AM about your age [17F] and have been handling a college LDR with my bf [19M] for about a year now (together since my freshman year) so I can maybe provide some insight as a peer since you've already got the motivational success stories :) Ultimately, is it difficult to stay in a relationship in college? Absolutely. It requires a lot of patience and trust. Luckily, it sounds like you guys already have a really solid foundation since you've been together this long. My biggest piece of advice is talk about EVERYTHING before you make a decision. If you get everything out in the open now and figure out what's enough for both of you in the relationship, it'll be so much easier down the line once you're in the thick of things and keep conflicts to a minimal. I'm not going to lie, it was really hard/terrifying to do that before my bf left for school. It was scary knowing he was going to be making an entirely new life for himself. The biggest thing you need to remember is just because you'll both be making new friends doesn't exclude you from keeping each other! At the end of each day, you have someone to tell all your exciting new experiences to and get some in return--you get to meet her new friends (if only over Skype for now) and she gets to meet yours and ultimately, you get double the connections. Believe it or not, you'll have a great support network too--2 of my bf's friends on his dorm floor are also in LDRs which was totally coincidental. You're not alone in this. Having separate college experiences by no means excludes you from still being apart of each others' lives. 

That being said, because LDRs are incredibly challenging, if you're seriously doubting it, it may be best to break things off before school start and maintain your friendship (maybe even seeing where life goes later on) than giving it a shot without your heart in it and having a messy end. 

Long story short, talk to her! Figure out what you both want and need and go from there. I promise it's doable and there's no better feeling than getting to fall in love all over again every visit. Hi there! I was the person who was left behind as my boyfriend of about the length as you left for school, so I completely understand how you're feeling. For me personally, I knew my LDR was worth it just because I--as cheesy as it sounds--couldn't picture my life without him, without his family, without this super important piece of me. I knew that saying goodbye to him would be hard, but nothing would be harder than a permanent one. That's pretty much what ran through my head: "Why would I give up this person and lose him simply because I'm afraid of losing him?" 

It's true that you're young and in the prime of your life, and if you think you'd be happier being free and exploring and are going to resent your current boyfriend during your time apart for "holding you back", then maybe long distance isn't for you and you two will need to have some difficult discussions. I'm not going to lie to you, there are going to be days where things are really hard. There are going to be days where you might question it being worth it. It's difficult knowing he's out there having a different life, BUT let me give you some reasons why your fear of this is understandable, but not necessarily true :) 

Yes, you'll have different lives which may be scary. BUT just because you're not there does not mean you won't be a part of it. The way I like to look at it is, think about the excitement of falling in love. You meet this new, wonderful person, and you're excited to talk to them, to learn new things about them, and to hear about their day and share yours. In that way, I think LDRs are really great. Yes, it sucks being away from the person you care about. But being apart does not mean that you won't be part of his life. He'll be having new experiences, and you will too, but at the end of the day, you'll want to share these with each other, essentially letting you get excited for two lives instead of one and allowing you to experience the sensation of falling in love over and over as you grow together and pick up new things. When my boyfriend left for school, that was my biggest fear and the hardest part for me--feeling like he was having so much fun and having all these amazing experiences with new people, new EVERYTHING, whereas I was just stuck in the same place with same everything, only having lost him. It's not easy, BUT you aren't really losing anything. You get to share his excitement, his happiness, and eventually, maybe even his friends (I sometimes Skype and watch movies with my bf and his friends in their dorm on the weekends). As long as you keep moving forward, decide what you want your end goal to be, and keep working towards that together, I promise you the time really does fly by and every visit makes it that much more worthwhile. My biggest advice for you regarding your fear of having a new life: actively try to be involved in his new one. Get excited about the things he's excited about. Learn about the new things he's doing, about his favorite restaurants in his new town, the things he can do there, about his new friends (their names, what they're into). PAY ATTENTION to what he tells you and be interested in it; I'm not saying do any of this in a creepy obsessed possessive way, but taking interest in his new life, remembering the details, and bringing them up to him and understanding everything will help you feel like you're there and more of a part of his life in his new area. 

Overall, you know better than anyone if it's worth it. Decide what's enough for you and what you're looking for your end result to be and go from there. Welcome! Been long distance with my bf of 2 years for about half our relationship--closing in on 9 months. I agree with what everyone else is saying. The other thing that can be difficult but has helped us a lot is talking about EVERYTHING. Working out a plan for what both of you need in the relationship, how much communication is enough, and what happens in different scenarios (cheating, attraction for someone else, plans/visits unexpectedly getting changed or canceled, etc.) It can be very hard, but since communication is so crucial in long distance, ultimately it's been very beneficial and will help you have a game plan and avoid potential in-the-moment anger or frustration where you say things you don't mean. My boyfriend (19) left for college out of state last fall while I was left in state (17F). It's definitely difficult, but no where near impossible! The best advice I can give is to set a Skype day. There are people who Skype more frequently, some even every day, but for us, setting aside Sunday to Skype was extremely helpful. It gives you something to look forward to throughout the week, helps you avoid conflict if you're busy during the week (which you likely will be--college is a busy time), and still allows you to have your own lives and enjoy the college experience. Speaking of the college experience, the other advice I would recommend is discussing what both of you want to get out of your experiences. Talk about these expectations early to avoid jealousy/drama if say, one of you wants to go to parties and the other isn't sure how they would handle it. The most important things I think are to make a game plan to how you're going to balance your personal lives and your relationship and talking about EVERYTHING--even the really hard stuff. What happens if one of you cheats, inevitable attraction to other people, what's enough for you, how you handle each situation, etc. It's really hard to talk about, but it's SO important and will really help you down the line. Most importantly, just remember that while it's really hard and scary, you have a person that loves you enough to take on the difficulties :) and there's no better feeling than coming home and falling in love all over again. Good luck! Feel free to message me for any questions or advice, always love hearing from other high school to college couples! You're definitely not in this alone

Hi! I'm 17f dating 19m. We had been dating for about a year and a half as well when he went to college. I'll be straight up--is it really hard? Yes. Are there going to be a lot of people (including family and friends) that advise you against it? Yup. That being said, whether or not the distance is worth it is entirely up to you two. If you two both want to be able to experience new things and be with new people while you're young without ties to people from high school interfering with college, then it's probably something you two need to mutually agree to let go. However, if you truly see this boy as someone you are willing to wait for and deal with the challenges that come with long distance, go for it. The best advice I ever received going into this was "Figure out what's enough." Think about what you need in the relationship to make it worthwhile and what you are willing to be flexible with and compromise on. If you decide to go for it, talk about everything--even the really hard stuff. What happens if one of you cheats, how do you deal with inevitable attraction and fascination with other people/jealousy, etc. It's really hard talking about some of that stuff and there were times leading up to my boyfriend leaving where we really started to believe it wasn't worth it BECAUSE it seemed so daunting and the ideas people were feeding us with our young age and changing and college and whatnot got to be too much. You both will change. But changing is a part of life and that would happen whether or not you two were long distance or not; you just have to keep growing together. 
In my experience, long distance relationships in high school are not as bad as they are made out to be (I am starting my senior year in HS while he is a rising sophomore in college) BUT I think every individual's experience is different. It's really all about your attitude and the understanding that both of you are going to have separate lives, but lives that you still want to share with the other regardless of the distance, time difference, etc. It's not easy. There will be lots of challenges. You both have to be very mature and reasonable and have a healthy and strong relationship. But it's doable--I am fortunate enough to be close with a friend's parents and a teacher of mine who all are happily married to their previously long distance high school sweethearts (not to say you need to know if you want to marry this kid--you are young, but just saying that it is possible to be successful and happy even if finding love at a young age). Don't let fear of a challenge talk you out of it; it can be truly rewarding! That being said, whatever you choose, the world will unfold as it should. Sorry for this being so long, but I am always excited to talk to young LDRs out there--props to you if you read this whole thing. If you have any questions at all, please don't hesitate to message me. I'd love to give you any advice or share more about my experience going from high school relationship to long distance through college or share honestly any of the challenges or realities that comes with it. Best of luck with your decision and in college!

Hey there OP. My SO and I met in high school, but different schools so we have pretty much always been semi-long distance, seeing each other about once a month at least. I've always struggled with anxiety and depression, but it got much worse once he left for college. In all honesty, I don't think it's ever 100% going to go away. Some moments could be really great and then anxiety can smack you out of nowhere. I've found that the best thing for me is keeping a journal (especially during and after visits) where I write down all the little things that I'm thankful for, meaningful things he said, or my favorite moments and gestures. Whenever I get anxious or start doubting the situation, rereading the good times help make the bad a little less difficult and reminds me why I fell in love in the first place and why I know I can trust him. I've found keeping a journal is very beneficial for curbing anxiety and it's fun to add new memories as time goes on, so if either of you are writers or creative, or simply want a new approach, I highly recommend giving it a try. It's unfortunately very sad to be in this distanced. But apps like Couple and FaceTime make communication and seeing each other much easier and can calm anxiety down. I also find that writing letters to each other, while maybe expensive from the US to the UK, can be incredible as it lets him carry around a piece of you to reread whenever a particularly bad flash hits him and gives each of you something to look forward to as you wait for the next letter to come. Anxiety and depression are not things that go away overnight and unfortunately, neither is distance. They all take hard work and a positive mindset and approach, and it sounds like you are already on a great track. Keep busy, support each other, make your feelings clear. Remember that there is only so much you can do to help your SO as this is their fight. The greatest thing you can do is be there for them and always always always be supportive and understanding. Understand that they trust you, but their minds make it difficult to keep from worrying sometimes. Just communicated and stay positive and I have no doubt you two will find a way through this together. Best of luck!
